title: Plus and minus chips
hook: Plus-chips and minus-chips cancel in pairs. What is your hand worth?

knows: counting and subtraction of whole numbers
doesNotKnow: negative numbers as opposites that cancel positives
why adding a negative is the same as subtracting

misconception: A negative number is just a positive one with a sign painted on, with no arithmetic meaning.
objective: The learner can explain that a plus and a minus together make zero, so 5 plus-chips and 3 minus-chips total 2, and 5 + (-3) = 5 - 3.

claims.text: 3 plus-chips and 5 minus-chips total -2: three pairs cancel and two minus-chips are left.
claims.source: 3 - 5 = -2; stage cancels 3 pairs leaving 2 minus-chips. The total readout stays '?' until only one kind of chip is left. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 11): 3 - 5 = -2; Demo.tsx readout shows "?" while canCancel (both kinds > 0), line 121.

claims.text: A plus-chip and a minus-chip together are worth zero, so cancelling a pair never changes the total.
claims.source: 1 + (-1) = 0 (additive inverse); removing a pair changes the total by -(1 + (-1)) = 0.

claims.text: A negative number is the opposite that cancels a positive one, like a debt against cash: 5 minus-chips are not worth +5, and 3 + (-5) = 3 - 5 = -2.
claims.source: Integers as additive inverses (a + (-a) = 0, a + (-b) = a - b). The chip picture is the two-colour counter model used in teaching integers, e.g. Van de Walle, Karp and Bay-Williams, Elementary and Middle School Mathematics, chapter on integers. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 11): Additive inverse a + (-a) = 0 and a + (-b) = a - b; two-colour counter model is a standard teaching model (Van de Walle et al.). Conventional, correct.

recall.question: Your wallet holds 4 one-pound coins and 6 one-pound IOUs. What is it worth?
recall.why: Each coin cancels one IOU. Four pairs make zero and two IOUs are left: 4 + (-6) = -2.
